business_problem: Tuiwen Technology had built AI systems for translating, generating, and distributing Chinese online literature overseas, but the platform needed much stronger monitoring and log retention as its scale grew. Containerized workloads were short-lived, logs could disappear with the containers, and the company needed a unified operations surface that could support both the AI pipeline and the surrounding export platform.
solution_summary: Tuiwen Technology runs its web-novel export business on Alibaba Cloud using ECS and Log Service SLS as the operational foundation beneath its AI translation and publishing systems. The company's AI translation-generation-distribution pipeline automatically monitors, fetches, translates, and publishes licensed Chinese novels, while a separate AI production-distribution system can package books for rapid digital release. Because the workload is containerized and integrates additional services such as Flink, Function Compute, and WAF, Tuiwen needed a logging system that could persist short-lived operational traces and unify them across many components. SLS became that collection and analysis plane: it ingests K8s logs, application logs, and related service logs, generates monitoring reports, and supports alerting into collaboration tools so a small engineering team can keep the high-volume AI content-export pipeline stable without staffing a much larger operations function.

solution_components.name: Elastic Compute Service (ECS)
solution_components.role: Provides the cloud compute layer that runs Tuiwen's AI-driven translation and publishing services.

solution_components.name: Log Service SLS
solution_components.role: Collects, retains, analyzes, and alerts on logs across containerized AI translation and distribution systems.

solution_components.name: AI translation generation distribution system
solution_components.role: Automatically monitors, grabs, translates, and publishes licensed Chinese web novels.

solution_components.name: AI production distribution system
solution_components.role: Packages and releases translated books at industrial scale for overseas channels.

data_flow: Licensed Chinese novels are detected and ingested by Tuiwen's AI translation platform, translated and prepared for distribution, and then published to overseas reading channels. Throughout that process, ECS runs the services while SLS captures logs from Kubernetes workloads and related components so failures, anomalies, and performance issues can be identified and acted on quickly.
business_outcome: Alibaba Cloud helped Tuiwen scale an AI-native content-export factory for online literature. The company can now translate and distribute content at industrial throughput while keeping platform operations manageable: the AI translation system reaches 3 seconds per chapter, 20 chapters per minute, and 20,000 to 30,000 chapters per day, while the AI publishing system can release 3,000+ books per month at far lower cost than manual workflows.
metrics: translation cost reduced to 1% of the original level
15 minutes per book for AI production and distribution
architecture_clues: The AI workflow is split between a translation-generation-distribution system and a separate production-distribution system.
Short-lived container logs are treated as a core operational risk, so centralized log collection is part of the architecture.
SLS aggregates logs not only from Kubernetes but also from adjacent services such as Flink, Function Compute, and WAF.
AI throughput and publishing throughput are both industrialized rather than handled as isolated translation jobs.
